name: Loeffler Randall
band_note: mean of blouse and sweater entry $288 (women's price pass, 2026-10-13)
why: Women's shoes (pleated-bow heels, ballet flats, boots), handbags and some ready-to-wear, shoes mostly $275–700, sold through its own stores and site, department stores and boutiques.
origin: Founded in Brooklyn, United States in 2004 by Jessie Randall; Brian Murphy.

quote.q: Since I was a little girl, a new pair of shoes has meant a feeling of pure and total joy.

doors.note: US: 4 own doors — SoHo (10 Prince St) and West Village (343 Bleecker St), New York; Charleston (145 King St); Nashville (2510 12th Ave S). World: plus London (44 Chiltern St), 5 in all, each with its own page and a matching row in the locator feed. The feed holds 273 points; 231 have a blank country field: 4 own stores, 3 John Lewis (UK) rows, and 224 US wholesale accounts (Nordstrom x33, Bloomingdale's x25, Dillard's x11 and many boutiques) in return_stockists.csv; the other 42 are abroad. Phones from the stores' call links. New York label.

craft_evidence.owned: no — SoHo design office (588 Broadway) and stores; 'factory technicians' mentioned, no factory named (/pages/about)
craft_evidence.madein: 0 of 80 clothing pages state a country
craft_evidence.heritage: founded 2004 in Cobble Hill by Jessie and Brian Randall, family-owned (/pages/about)
craft_evidence.process: partial, for shoes only — '28 steps' and '400 pleats' in the Penny heel, 40 hand mock-ups a season, 3 fittings per style; nothing on how the clothing is made
craft_evidence.reasoning: For the clothing, nothing names a maker, place or process, and product pages state no country; the dated founding and the shoe-making steps on the about page do not reach the apparel. 1 (the shoe process would argue a 2 for the brand as a whole).
